source.title: Gradient Transformer: Learning to Generate Updates for LLMs
source.authors: B. Nguyen; Khang Tran; Nhathai Phan; Issa M. Khalil

page_placements.theme: Transferring a weaker model's training shift (RL policy shift, update vectors, contrast against a weaker predictor) to a stronger model

record.file_problem: None; the text includes the paper and appendices. Some table content is flattened, making individual method-to-value assignments unclear.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates Burns et al.'s weak-to-strong fine-tuning baselines, including W2S and its confidence-loss variant, and reports PGR. These are baseline experiments within a paper primarily proposing a different update-vector transfer method.
record.gate_note: The paper names W2S and Conf as baselines and describes their training procedures. Table 1 contains flattened values that cannot be reliably assigned to individual methods and tasks, so those values are not extracted as method-specific results. The paper's proposed update-vector method is not weak-label fine-tuning; its results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The paper runs Burns et al.'s naive weak-to-strong fine-tuning (W2S) and its auxiliary-confidence variant (Conf), plus VisSup, as baselines. It uses a Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct weak supervisor and a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct student on six generative reasoning and summarization tasks, and reports per-task PGR. Its own Grad-Transformer is not weak-label fine-tuning; those results fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude Grad-Transformer outperforms the weak-to-strong baselines (W2S, Conf, VisSup) without accessing client data, including under strict DP. They concede logit-based baselines win on some datasets, and that performance depends on public/private data alignment. They draw no conclusion about weak-to-strong generalization itself.
record.recipe_differences: The paper includes the original weak-label fine-tuning baseline and the auxiliary-confidence variant, using Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on downstream tasks. Its main proposed method instead maps TinyLM parameter updates to LLM updates.
record.method_sensitivity: For the proposed update-vector method, results vary with public-shadow dataset size and alignment, update-vector segmentation, client task mix, and DP-SGD privacy level. Weak-label baseline method sensitivity is not reliably extractable from the flattened tables.

fits_no_version.finding: Grad-Transformer reaches average PGR of 91.88% (single client), 85.01% (five clients) and 88.02% under DP-SGD with epsilon 0.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mapping a small model's fine-tuning update vectors to a larger model's updates can recover most of the performance gap without weak-label training.

record.problems: Weak-to-strong baseline values in Table 1 are flattened and cannot be reliably assigned to each method and task. The prose gives aggregate PGR for Conf but no uncertainty estimates. The paper's main method is parameter-update transfer, so its results do not directly establish the behavior of weak-label fine-tuning.
record.rows_left_out: Individual W2S, Conf, and VisSup values in Tables 1 and 3 were left out where flattened layout did not support reliable assignment to a method, task, or client. The paper's proposed-method table values beyond the explicitly reported aggregates were also not expanded into rows.

untested.parts: Only one supervisor/student pair (3B to 7B) is used for the baselines.
Size dependence of baseline PGR and representation-based predictors are not tested. Table 2 scales only the paper's own method.
Not tested: exploitation, shared errors, distribution shift for weak-label fine-tuning.
Not tested; the theory concerns Grad-Transformer bounds.

missing.what: Per-task naive W2S PGR for single client. AQuA -46.24, GSM8K 86.34, DROP 18.86, CQA 82.13, SAMSum 68.47, DialogSum 12.69; average 37.04. Recoverable from Table 1 accuracies with PS/PT.
Per-task Conf PGR for single client: -7.72, 110.82, 49.95, 94.98, 77.29, 28.29.
Multi-client average PGR per task for W2S/Conf/VisSup. AQuA 15.38/34.70/31.75; CQA 68.04/63.92/68.04; DROP 63.85/83.00/69.02; SAMSum 59.71/98.24/84.41.
VisSup (adaptive confidence loss) vs W2S PGR. It is higher on most tasks but lower on single-client DialogSum (5.57 vs 12.69).

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 is not unrecoverable: the column order can be reconstructed and PGRs check against the accuracies, e.g. W2S AQuA (43.70-48.43)/(58.66-48.43) = -46.2. Baselines are single runs with no uncertainty. The tasks are generative, with exact-match or ROUGE scoring, so this is a new setting relative to the original classification tasks. The weak model is trained on one half of the training data and labels the other half, as in Burns et al. V3 is touched only by variation across tasks: W2S PGR ranges from -46 to 86. That spread is noted in missing, not given a label, since task-sensitivity is described rather than tested against a predictor.

versions.untested_parts: W2S is evaluated, but its method-specific PGR values cannot be reliably assigned from the flattened Table 1. No W2S results by client are stated in prose.
The paper reports the average PGR for Conf and identifies it as the best-performing baseline, but does not provide an unambiguous extracted W2S-versus-Conf comparison for each task or client.
The W2S baselines are evaluated across tasks, but task-specific PGR values cannot be reliably assigned from Table 1. Size and representation effects on weak-label fine-tuning PGR are not tested.
No weak-label student exploitability, shared-error effects, or distribution-shift effects on weak-label fine-tuning are tested.
The theoretical analysis concerns generalization and utility bounds for the proposed update-vector method, not conditions that require a student to outperform its weak-label supervisor.
Vision results are not reported; Vision Superalignment is named as a baseline but its own experiments are not conducted here.
